provider: Bundesarchiv, distributed through Deutsche Digitale Bibliothek
source_kind: Institutional fonds description and catalogue history; the underlying archival business plans were not inspected
retrieval_scope: Official catalogue text returned by search; direct page fetch presented a bot challenge and was not treated as content evidence
paraphrase: The institutional history lists A VI S as the maritime transport division in the 1914 organization. Its account of the 1917 business plan lists A.VI as that division, with subsidiary offices for auxiliary ships, naval transport, army and colonial-force transport, and administration.
inference: The A6S office string in the ship-sale telegrams is consistent with the maritime transport office. This supports the office interpretation independently of those ciphertexts.
limits: Institutional catalogue evidence is not a scan of the contemporary business plan.
This does not authenticate the ship-sale telegram or establish that every related damaged office field was copied correctly.
The assumptions linking specific office fields and their numerical labels remain conditional.
The published keys and existing source/cipher certificates are unchanged.
